clue.text: Short, opening passage in trombone solo

indicators.note: short here means a cut-down stretch, so only the front portion of the words in trombone is taken

explanation.surface: A brief opening phrase played by a trombonist in a solo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' signals that only the opening letters of 'in trombone' are used, run together across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the introductory section of a piece of music, its opening passage.

clue.text: Do such people have an aim? Register one charity first

parts.note: an aim or plan is an idea
a register is a list
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: first here asks for the opening letter of the word charity

explanation.surface: A question about whether some people have a goal, followed by a reminder to sign up for a charity.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the playful question 'Do such people have (an aim)?': idealistic people have ideals, and the aim itself supplies IDEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealistic people are guided by lofty goals, which is the sort of person the question asks about.

clue.text: A devil of a place for ferocious animals!

definitions.text: A devil of a place for ferocious animals!

parts.words: A devil of a place for ferocious animals!
parts.note: reads as a hellish spot full of wild beasts, but points to the Australian island state that gives its name to a famously fierce marsupial devil

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a terrible place overrun by savage beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tasmanian devil is a snarling carnivorous marsupial found only on this Australian island, so 'a devil of a place' is literally a place of devils.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian island state is home to the ferocious Tasmanian devil.

clue.text: Team, accepted by overdrawn workers, cause rust

definitions.note: a verb phrase; the answer is the plural noun naming the things that cause rust

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside, so the team sits within the letters for overdrawn

parts.note: OD is the bank-statement abbreviation for overdrawn
a cricket or football team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals
worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: A team is taken on by indebted labourers who make things corrode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted by' puts XI inside OD to give OXID, then ANTS follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxidants are agents that oxidise metals, which is how iron rusts.

clue.text: Even half the caves around the lake are enclosures

indicators.note: half here takes the back two letters of the four-letter word even
around means the word caves wraps itself about the letter for lake

parts.note: L is the standard map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Half the caves around a lake are fenced-off areas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even half' gives EN, the back half of EVEN; 'around' then puts L inside CAVES to make CLAVES.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclave is a territory enclosed within another, so enclaves are enclosed areas.

clue.text: Other fella seen regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every second letter of fella seen, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Another bloke is spotted at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of 'fella seen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Else means other or different, as in 'someone else'.

clue.text: Got to know Shakespearean king at the national theatre

parts.note: King Lear is the title king of Shakespeare's tragedy
NT stands for the National Theatre, the London playhouse on the South Bank

explanation.surface: Someone became familiar with King Lear at the National Theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Theatre is Britain's state-funded theatre company in London, abbreviated NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Learnt is the past tense of learn, meaning came to know.

clue.text: Plant full of nothing but veins

definitions.note: a plural noun; the answer is the adjective meaning of or full of veins

indicators.note: full of means the plant's name holds the letter for nothing inside it

parts.note: Venus is the short name of the Venus flytrap, the meat-eating plant
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A plant that contains nothing except its veins.
explanation.walkthrough: The Venus flytrap is commonly just called Venus; 'full of' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Venous describes blood vessels returning to the heart, or a leaf marked with many veins.

clue.text: There are usually up to three or five in court

definitions.text: There are usually up to three or five in court

parts.words: There are usually up to three or five in court
parts.note: sounds like a legal hearing, but the court is a tennis court where a match is decided over a best of three or five units

explanation.surface: A remark about how many people usually appear in a court of law.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennis matches are played as best of three or best of five of these divisions.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a match is divided into sets, usually three for women and five in men's majors.

clue.text: Designer seating for special courses taken to the right, usually

definitions.text: courses taken to the right, usually

indicators.note: designer means remodelled or styled anew, so the letters of seating are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stylish seating arranged for particular routes heading right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Designer' signals rearranging SEATING into EASTING, and S follows. On a standard map east is to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastings are distances travelled eastward, which on a north-up map runs rightward.

clue.text: Huge moose run all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered, so the letters of moose and run are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A huge moose runs wild in every direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' rearranges the eight letters of MOOSE and RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous is a synonym of huge, meaning very large.

clue.text: Anne sets changing standards of tidiness

indicators.note: changing means the letters of Anne and sets alter their order

explanation.surface: A woman named Anne alters the standards for keeping things tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges the eight letters of ANNE and SETS; 'standards of' links them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatness is the quality of being orderly and tidy.

clue.text: Escape of general loaded with a kilo of silver

indicators.note: loaded with means the general's name is packed with the following letters

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the American Confederate general
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver, from Latin argentum

explanation.surface: A general weighed down with a kilo of silver makes a getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded with' puts A, K and AG inside LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A leakage is an escape of liquid or gas through a gap.

clue.text: The outflow of notes spoken competently

indicators.note: spoken means the musical note letter is written as it is pronounced

parts.note: F is a musical note
fluent means able to speak competently and smoothly

explanation.surface: Musical notes delivered with skill as they flow out.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter F said aloud is spelt EF; FLUENT then follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Effluent is liquid waste discharged into a river or sea, an outflow.

clue.text: Musicians list Faust as awkward

indicators.note: awkward means clumsily placed, so the letters of list and Faust are reordered

explanation.surface: Musicians awkwardly list Faust, the character of opera and legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' rearranges the nine letters of LIST and FAUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Flautists are players of the flute, a kind of musician.

clue.text: Desert blow-ups

parts.note: sounds like explosions or angry quarrels in the desert, but means violent winds whipping up sand in arid lands

explanation.surface: Explosions or rows out in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow-ups' suggests explosions or tantrums, but here it means storms that blow up.
explanation.definitionFit: Storms of wind-driven sand sweep across deserts, blowing up suddenly.

clue.text: Interchange of organ across the estate

parts.note: trans is the Latin prefix meaning across
a plantation is a large farming estate

explanation.surface: Moving an organ from place to place across an estate.
explanation.walkthrough: TRANS- is the prefix meaning across, as in transatlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Transplantation is the surgical moving of an organ from one body to another.

clue.text: Progressed air defence vehicle with chief engineer's department

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
CE stands for chief engineer

explanation.surface: An air-defence vehicle moved forward, alongside the chief engineer's section.
explanation.walkthrough: A string of military-style abbreviations: AD, VAN, CE and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Advanced means moved forward or made progress.

clue.text: Personal admission contrary to being imperishable

parts.note: a personal admission is a statement about yourself that begins 'I'm'
a mortal is a human being

explanation.surface: Confessing 'I'm mortal' runs contrary to claiming to be undying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrary to' links the pieces to the definition; saying 'I'm mortal' is indeed the opposite of being imperishable.
explanation.definitionFit: Immortal means living forever, never perishing.

clue.text: Continuous but doesn't notice as much, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the phrase is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: someone who notices less sees less

explanation.surface: An observation that something constant is noticed less and less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sees less' said aloud sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceaseless means never stopping, continuous.

clue.text: High fliers remain up in the sky

indicators.note: up in the sky suggests letters tossed about in the air, so remain is rearranged

explanation.surface: Pilots stay airborne high above.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up in the sky' rearranges REMAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen are pilots or air-force crew, people who fly high.

clue.text: More than singular runs

parts.note: extra means more, additional
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Runs that number more than one.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, extras are runs not scored off the bat, such as byes and wides.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, extras are runs added for byes, wides and no-balls.

clue.text: Outdoor activity around each harbour

indicators.note: around means the outdoor activity surrounds the letters for each

parts.note: sport is an outdoor activity

explanation.surface: Outdoor games played around each harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts EA inside SPORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaport is a town with a harbour for ships.

clue.text: Provoke one bishop to visit international gallery

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A bishop is provoked into visiting an international art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: A bishop is styled the Right Reverend, abbreviated RR; the Tate is a group of British national art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: To irritate is to annoy or provoke.

clue.text: Poetry division originally in all Milton's books

indicators.note: originally means taking the opening letter of in, all, Milton's and books

explanation.surface: A unit of poetry that appears in every one of Milton's books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes the first letter of each of the four words.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical foot, a short syllable then a long, used throughout Milton's verse.

clue.text: Recognise up to over fifty fish

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second
in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to see is to recognise
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone recognises ages up to fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SEE into EES, and 'over' places it above L.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long snake-like fish.

clue.text: Playfully courted a teacher

indicators.note: playfully means jokingly rearranged, so the letters of courted and a are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone flirtatiously wooed a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playfully' rearranges COURTED and A.
explanation.definitionFit: An educator is a teacher, someone who educates.

clue.text: Ben initially ingratiated with relatives' blessings

indicators.note: initially means just the opening letter of the word ingratiated

parts.note: sons are male relatives

explanation.surface: Ben first wins over his relatives and receives their blessings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes I from 'ingratiated'.
explanation.definitionFit: A benison is a blessing, an old-fashioned word for a benediction.

clue.text: Deep hollows caused by toboggan backing over the line

indicators.note: over means placed covering, so the turned toboggan sits over the letter for line
backing means going in reverse, so the word for a toboggan is turned round

parts.note: a sled is a toboggan

explanation.surface: Deep hollows gouged by a toboggan reversing across the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns SLED into DELS, and 'over' wraps it round L.
explanation.definitionFit: A dell is a small wooded valley or hollow.
